Chapter 10: Sustaining Change—Review, Reflect, and Realign.
So, here we are at the heart of making change stick—ongoing reflection. Real, lasting change doesn’t just happen overnight. It’s built through regular check-ins, honest reflection, and those gentle tweaks along the way.
Think about it like this: taking time to pause and really look at how you’re spending your days gives you a chance to celebrate your wins, catch yourself if you start drifting, and make sure you’re still aligned with what matters most to you.
Reflection doesn’t have to be complicated. Maybe it’s a quick weekly review, jotting down a few notes in a journal, or just taking a quiet walk to mull over what’s been working—and what hasn’t. The goal isn’t to judge yourself, but to learn and gently adjust.
Here’s a simple way to approach it:
First, look back at your week. Maybe flip through your calendar or check your time log. Notice which activities felt especially meaningful or left you feeling energized. Are there any places where you lost track of your priorities, or things started to drift off course?
Now, set one or two small intentions for the week ahead. Nothing huge—just little adjustments to help you course-correct.
For example, let’s say you realize that family dinners have slipped because work meetings keep running late. That’s a great insight! Maybe you decide to set a firmer boundary and protect that dinner time a bit more moving forward. Over time, these small shifts really start to add up. Life gradually becomes more aligned, more intentional.
And here’s something to pay attention to: regular reflection doesn’t just help you realign. It actually builds self-awareness and gratitude. When you notice what’s going well, it’s a lot easier to stay motivated and resilient—even when things get tough.
So, the process becomes a gentle cycle. Plan, act, reflect, and realign. That’s how sustainable change truly takes root.
